description: A modular, stack-agnostic toolkit for AI coding agents to autonomously find, reproduce, and patch vulnerabilities.

written.description: Reads a codebase and its commit history, builds a threat model from them, and sends agents to chase each hypothesis it raises. It then tries to reproduce each finding in a sandbox and attacks its own patch to check the fix holds, working from source alone with no running target.

alive.last_commit_message:
Close the findings of the October security review

An automated review of the reference harness (eight attack-surface
hunters, each finding verified by an adversarial proof of concept)
reported eighteen confirmed weaknesses. Sixteen are closed here, each
pinned by a test in tests/test_security_review_2026_10.py named for its
report number; the other two are design questions recorded below.

The MCP server kept its state in <repo>/.mantis/ -- inside the code
under audit. A committed symlink at a predictable path there turned the
resolutions log, scan logs and index writes into writes to any file the
server's user could reach, and a committed knowledge.db plus catalog
was trusted as the server's own memory, enough to hand `--check` a PASS
on a never-scanned file. State now lives in a per-repository directory
outside the checkout (<workspace>/mcp/<hash>, MANTIS_MCP_STATE_DIR, or
--state-dir); a state directory inside the repository is refused, and
logs are opened without following symlinks. Scans are bounded: at most
50 files per call, 500 model calls per pipeline, two running at once.

Reached-sink evidence (INV-1) accepted any crash-like text anywhere in
output -- a changelog line saying "fixed Segmentation fault", read by an
honest model with `cat`, promoted findings to dynamic_confirmed -- and
matched a sink symbol as a plain substring. A crash must now be
corroborated by a sanitizer report, a signal exit, or a non-zero exit
with a backtrace, and a sink symbol must be named by a parsed frame.
The fixed sentinel string remains forgeable by a model that writes the
proof of concept; that is a design limit of the deterministic channel,
not a patch, and the controls that matter there are separation of
duties and re-attack.

Model-filled fields could claim verification on their own.
patch_status VERIFIED_SECURE was kept whenever the model also wrote
reattack_status failed_to_bypass, so a static-only run exported a
"verified" patch; write_findings now also requires the harness's own
record that the sandbox reached a sink this run. A synthesized or
hand-written workflow could stamp patch_verified on node completion,
which the change gate treats as closed; nodes may stamp only
static_confirmed and dynamic_confirmed, enforced where the stamp is
attached. Re-reporting a finding with FALSE_POSITIVE demoted a
dynamic_confirmed row and blanked its verified patch, and re-reporting
a dismissed one as VALID revived it; the monotonic guard now applies to
the row actually rewritten, for every incoming status. merge_findings
took model-chosen ids with no run scope and no terminal clause, so one
call from run A merged a patch_verified finding in run B; every
statement is now scoped to the run and guarded.

Two files under the size cap could stall or exhaust the index build: a
chained call was walked quadratically (and resolved to the wrong name --
a.b.c() called 'b'), nesting depth grew qualified names quadratically,
a FIFO blocked read_bytes forever, and the size cap was checked after
reading, so a sparse multi-gigabyte file was read whole. The callee
walk follows the right spine in constant work, depth and name length
are capped, staging admits regular files only, and size is checked on
the inode first.

Smaller closures: the citation verifier applied none of read_file's
gates and so answered existence, line count and identifier presence for
files read_file refuses (sibling files in a single-file scan, symlink
aliases of .git/config, case variants), and os.path.isdir ran on
model-supplied paths host-wide; both now bound to the jail with the
same gates, and a protected-name check is case-insensitive. --resume
replaced the validated scan target with a stored finding path without
re-validation; it may now only narrow inside the validated target. The
declarative custom tool opened the database at a CWD-relative path,
creating files in the target; it resolves through the same anchor as
every other access and opens read-only. The executable custom tool
quoted the model's path but let `--output=...` through as an option;
options, absolute paths and traversal are refused. get_findings,
get_plan, get_threat_model and get_summary returned model-written text
to the gate stages unfenced; they carry the same untrusted-data fence
as every other model-to-model channel. SARIF export skipped the egress
sanitizer, so credentials the model quoted left in the file and a
description could forge the verification note; both fixed.

Not changed, by design: the fixed sentinel token (above), and target
file names in the seed prompt, which would change every node's seed
contract for a low-severity, prompt-level gain; both are recorded for a
later design pass.

Change-Id: Ib6ed7d9966fbe653bba98c83c2de69a12b1483a7
